parallel.requirements: Recognized the need for a pure JavaScript Node.js ESM migration in .mjs files, exact JWT output, manual process.argv parsing, Python-style dict repr, no external packages, and direct probing through /workspace/dataset/test8_executable.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Although swarm mode was injected, the main agent declared the task too small and tightly coupled for subagents, kept all implementation, integration, and verification ownership locally, and executed no child-agent mechanism.
parallel.implementation: Implemented pure-JS SHA-256, HMAC, base64url helpers, Python-compatible JSON and repr helpers, a minimal JWT surface, a minimal argparse parser, and /output/test8.mjs.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Wrote all modules directly under /output and produced the expected entry file; artifact validation later listed test8.mjs and the lib modules as copied successfully.
parallel.verification: Compared sample cases, unicode/escape cases, empty values, --arg=value, control characters, an astral emoji, help output, and several stderr paths against the executable, but accepted program-name stderr differences.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation still failed 20 of 70 cases; the direct trajectory leaves the exact hidden-case defect unresolved and contains no delegated work or parallel result to inspect.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same ESM, .mjs, argv, exact output, no dependency, no Python-command, and black-box executable requirements from the identical prompt.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Used a single main-agent path with local probing, module authoring, parser repair, verification, and final delivery; no subagents or delegated scopes were present.
serial.implementation: Implemented pure-JS SHA-256, HMAC-SHA256, base64url, UTF-8, JSON, Python repr, JWT helpers, manual argparse, and the /output/test8.mjs entry file.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Wrote the modules under /output, then edited argparse.mjs after testing exposed a mismatch; artifact validation later listed test8.mjs and all serial lib modules as copied successfully.
serial.verification: Ran sample comparisons, special-character checks, an option-like value test that initially failed, normalized CLI error/help checks after the fix, and 30 random fuzz inputs.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation still failed 20 of 70 cases despite broader local tests; no serial-control violation or unfinished delegated work appears.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel identified pure ESM .mjs output, manual CLI parsing, exact stdout, zero external dependencies, and black-box executable probing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial received and followed the same prompt requirements, including ESM, .mjs output, manual argv parsing, and executable-based observation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement recognition gap is evident; both attempted the same core obligations and both officially failed 50/70.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel mode injected swarm instructions, but the main agent chose to do the small, tightly coupled task directly and owned all stages itself.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial mode had a conventional single-agent flow and the main agent owned probing, implementation, parser repair, testing, and delivery.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The observable ownership model was effectively the same single-owner strategy; the parallel side did not actually create a multi-agent decomposition.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: No child brief, cross-agent contract, or handoff boundary existed; protocol validation reports zero agent_swarm_calls, direct_agent_calls, subagent_ids, and delegation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial control likewise had no child interfaces or handoffs and no serial-control violation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There is no cross-agent context-transfer difference to explain either failed outcome.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote a hand-rolled pure-JS JWT stack and argparse parser; its argparse implementation rejected only a following token that started with -- when checking missing values.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote a similar stack, then edited argparse.mjs to add looksLikeOption so option-like values starting with - were handled more like argparse.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial made one concrete implementation improvement to argument parsing after observing a mismatch; parallel did not make that specific parser repair, but this was ordinary single-agent implementation behavior.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: All produced results were local tool outputs visible to the main agent; there were no child results, joins, trapped verifier findings, or late returned implementations.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial likewise had local tool outputs only; the main agent consumed the failed edge-case result, edited code, retested, and returned a final answer.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No parallel result lifecycle boundary exists; the only lifecycle contrast is serial's additional local repair loop.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote all deliverables directly into /output and artifact validation copied the expected entry and library files successfully.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also wrote directly into /output and artifact validation copied its expected entry and library files successfully.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No shared-state collision, overwrite, or contamination is visible; both have successful artifact collection with different but coherent module names.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verified four samples plus unicode, empty, --arg=value, control-character, astral, help, and error-path cases, but did not perform a fuzz loop or fix the program-name stderr mismatch.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial verified samples and edge cases, observed an option-like argument failure, repaired argparse, reran normalized error/help checks, and performed a 30-input fuzz run with zero local mismatches.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial had broader acceptance-style local testing and one repair cycle; official evaluation nevertheless graded both attempts identically at 50/70.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel completed normally without timeout in 338.666 agent seconds and closed with a final response claiming verified completion.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed normally without timeout in 456.395 agent seconds and closed after more local verification and fuzzing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Neither run shows deadline pressure, cancellation, or budget exhaustion; serial spent longer on additional local checks but the outcome stayed the same.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluations are not discordant: both the parallel-mode and serial-mode attempts failed at 50 of 70 cases. The concrete task-solving difference is that serial performed an additional option-like argument repair and fuzz pass after detecting a mismatch, while parallel kept its initial parser and tested a narrower edge set. Because the parallel trajectory did not actually execute any child-agent or multi-agent mechanism, that difference is an ordinary single-agent implementation and verification difference rather than a parallel coordination failure.
parallel_contributors: No parallel-side coordination contributor is present because actual_parallel_used is false and protocol validation found no delegation.
serial_contributors: Serial performed a local parser repair and broader verification loop, but this did not change the official pass/fail outcome.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial patched option-like value handling with looksLikeOption after a failed check; parallel only checked startsWith('--') in the initial parser and did not make the same repair.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; ordinary implementation and verification differences only
